diet.text: Young: cold-blooded prey; adults: warm-blooded prey and snakes

overview.text: The Patagonia Green Racer is a rear-fanged, mildly venomous snake of South America east of the Andes. Despite its name, most of its range is outside Patagonia.

identification.text: Medium-sized and fairly sturdy, brownish, with a rounded snout, round pupils and smooth scales.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Up to about 150 cm; females are bulkier, males have longer tails.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

habitat.text: Open country: Patagonian steppe, Cerrado, Chaco, Caatinga and open parts of the Atlantic forest.

behaviour.text: Active by day; it lives on the ground but climbs when foraging.

diet.text: Eats other snakes, even its own species. Young ones eat cold-blooded animals, adults warm-blooded ones.
